q: בת 78, מאושפזת במחלקה לסיעוד מורכב עקב פצעי לחץ מרובים. איזו מההתערבויות התזונתיות הבאות הוכחה כמשפרת ריפוי פצעי לחץ באופן משמעותי?
o: תוספת טיפול בויטמינים A,E,D ו-K
כלכלה פומית עשירת אנרגיה וחלבון
תוספת אבץ וויטמינים מקבוצה B
כלכלה אנטרלית בזונדה
explanation:
Repairing a pressure injury requires energy for healing and amino acids to build tissue. Inadequate intake is associated with slower healing and greater wound severity.

**Provide energy- and protein-rich food or oral supplements.** Daily healing targets of 30–35 kcal/kg and 1.3–1.5 g protein/kg can guide an individualized plan for an undernourished patient.

**A. Vitamins A, E, D and K.** Correct demonstrated or suspected deficiencies. Giving several vitamins alone leaves energy and protein needs unmet.
**B. Energy- and protein-rich oral intake.** Oral intake is preferred when feasible, and supplements can help patients reach both targets.
**C. Zinc and B vitamins.** Zinc occurs in some enriched nutritional formulas. A micronutrient combination alone has a different nutritional purpose and lacks evidence of the same healing benefit.
**D. Nasogastric feeding.** Tube feeding can support selected patients whose oral intake is inadequate. It has shown inconsistent benefit for pressure-injury healing and introduces aspiration and tube-related risks.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 692.

q: A 75-year-old woman with chronic anemia from myelodysplastic syndrome previously had no symptoms at a low baseline hemoglobin. Her hemoglobin is now 7.6 g/dL, with new chest pain and dyspnea on minimal exertion consistent with end-organ ischemia. Which transfusion approach matches Hazzard’s discussion on page 1480?
o: Wait until hemoglobin falls below 7 g/dL, applying the general-population threshold.
Transfuse with clinical individualization, applying the threshold for symptomatic end-organ ischemia.
Wait until hemoglobin falls below her chronic baseline, relying on her previous tolerance.
Transfuse toward a fixed age-based hemoglobin target, using chronological age to set the goal.
explanation:
Red-cell transfusion rapidly increases oxygen-carrying capacity. A patient who tolerated chronic anemia can still develop ischemia when oxygen delivery no longer meets demand.

**Transfuse promptly and individualize further treatment because new chest pain and dyspnea at 7.6 g/dL indicate end-organ ischemia in this case.**

**A. Wait for 7 g/dL.** A general restrictive threshold does not account for the new ischemic symptoms.
**B. Transfuse for symptomatic end-organ ischemia.** At 7.6 g/dL she is below the 8 g/dL threshold used here for symptomatic ischemia. Evaluate the new chest pain urgently for acute coronary syndrome and reassess the clinical response to transfusion.
**C. Use her previous tolerance.** The change from her usual symptom-free state makes the previous baseline an unreliable guide today.
**D. Use an age-based target.** Comorbidity, ischemia and response guide decisions. Chronological age supplies no fixed replacement target.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1480.

q: A 72-year-old woman with advanced pancreatic cancer is being considered for chemotherapy. Geriatric assessment identifies mild cognitive impairment, falls, polypharmacy, and poor nutritional status. What is the purpose of the CARG model described in Hazzard?
o: Estimate the probability of tumor response using patient and treatment variables
Estimate the risk of cancer mortality using patient and treatment variables
Estimate the risk of chemotherapy toxicity using patient and treatment variables
Estimate the probability of surgical recovery using patient and treatment variables
explanation:
The Cancer and Aging Research Group model combines patient factors, laboratory results and the planned regimen. **It estimates the risk of severe toxicity from chemotherapy.**

**A. Tumor response** — Tumor biology and drug sensitivity help predict shrinkage. CARG does not predict that endpoint.
**B. Cancer mortality** — Death from progressive cancer is a different outcome from a severe treatment complication.
**C. Chemotherapy toxicity** — Treatment intensity and measured vulnerabilities jointly influence the probability of serious adverse effects, helping the clinician discuss risk before treatment.
**D. Surgical recovery** — Recovery after an operation depends on the procedure, healing and rehabilitation. CARG was developed for chemotherapy.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1388.
ref: Hazzard Ch 88 — CANCER AND AGING: GENERAL PRINCIPLES

q: An 82-year-old man taking rivaroxaban develops severe bleeding. Alongside stabilization and assessment of the bleeding source, which agent does Hazzard describe as a decoy protein that binds and sequesters factor Xa inhibitors?
o: Intravenous treatment with idarucizumab
Intravenous treatment with andexanet alfa
Intravenous treatment with vitamin K
Intravenous treatment with protamine sulfate
explanation:
The recombinant, inactive factor Xa decoy described in the chapter is **andexanet alfa**. It binds factor Xa inhibitors such as rivaroxaban. This is a mechanism question. US sales ended in December 2025 after the FDA reported serious thrombotic safety concerns.

**A. Idarucizumab.** This antibody fragment specifically binds dabigatran.
**B. Andexanet alfa.** The modified factor Xa protein sequesters factor Xa inhibitors. Actual emergency reversal follows local protocols and drug availability.
**C. Vitamin K.** It supports synthesis of vitamin K-dependent clotting factors in warfarin reversal.
**D. Protamine sulfate.** It reverses unfractionated heparin and partially reverses low-molecular-weight heparin.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1522. FDA, Update on the Safety of Andexxa, December 2025.

q: An 86-year-old woman with severe aortic stenosis is not a candidate for valve replacement. The heart team discusses balloon aortic valvuloplasty as a palliative option. What role does Hazzard describe for this procedure?
o: Providing a durable replacement for the diseased aortic valve
Preventing recurrent stenosis by stopping valve calcification
Providing temporary symptom relief or a bridge to treatment
Providing lasting survival improvement comparable to valve replacement
explanation:
Balloon aortic valvuloplasty inflates a balloon across the stenotic valve to separate portions of the calcified leaflets. The native valve remains in place.
**Balloon dilation can relieve symptoms temporarily or stabilize a patient until definitive valve replacement.**

**A. Durable replacement.** Dilation leaves the diseased valve in place. It does not implant a prosthesis.
**B. Prevents recurrent stenosis.** The underlying calcium remains. Restenosis commonly occurs within six to twelve months.
**C. Temporary relief or bridge.** A modestly larger opening may improve symptoms in a nonsurgical candidate or stabilize an acutely decompensated patient before replacement.
**D. Lasting survival benefit comparable to replacement.** Reported one-year mortality was 35% to 50% after balloon dilation alone. Its role is relief or bridging.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1152, percutaneous aortic valvuloplasty.

q: A 76-year-old man has gait disturbance and paresthesias and is found to have vitamin B12 deficiency. His blood count shows neither anemia nor macrocytosis. How should the absent hematologic findings be interpreted?
o: Absent anemia does not exclude neurologic manifestations of the deficiency.
Absent anemia indicates that the deficiency has no neurologic significance.
Absent macrocytosis supports postponing replacement of the deficient vitamin.
Absent macrocytosis supports replacing folate instead of vitamin B12.
explanation:
B12 deficiency has neurologic and hematologic manifestations that need not appear together. **Gait impairment and paresthesias can be caused by B12 deficiency despite normal hemoglobin and cell size.**

**A. Neurologic disease without anemia** — Peripheral neuropathy and impaired position sense may occur before, or without, the expected blood-count abnormalities.
**B. No anemia means no neurologic effect** — The blood count cannot assess the integrity of peripheral nerves or posterior columns.
**C. No macrocytosis justifies delay** — Prompt treatment matters when neurologic injury is suspected because some deficits can persist.
**D. Give folate instead** — Folate does not replace cobalamin or treat B12-related neurologic injury.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 419–420, clinical features of B12 deficiency and Table 30-7.
ref: Hazzard Ch 30 — NUTRITION DISORDERS, OBESITY , AND ENTERAL/PARENTERAL ALIMENTATION

q: At admission to a care setting, the Braden scale is used to assess pressure-injury risk. What is the purpose of this assessment and subsequent reassessment?
o: Identify risk and tailor preventive interventions
Determine wound depth and stage existing tissue loss
Choose an antibiotic and document infection response
Determine the need for debridement and measure dead tissue
explanation:
Risk assessment and wound assessment answer different clinical questions. The Braden scale identifies factors that make pressure injury more likely and can be repeated as those risks change.

**Use the score to identify individual risks and tailor preventive care.** Admission screening followed by reassessment catches changes such as reduced mobility or falling intake.

**A. Identify risk and tailor prevention.** Match interventions to the findings, including offloading, skin protection and nutrition support.
**B. Stage an existing wound.** Stage depends on the deepest tissue affected on examination of the wound.
**C. Select an antibiotic.** Signs of invasive infection and appropriate cultures guide antimicrobial decisions.
**D. Measure dead tissue for debridement.** Assess the wound bed, perfusion, necrosis and indications for removal directly. The risk score measures none of these.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 682–683, 688–689.

q: בן 78, מהנדס במקצוע, בגמלאות, אלמן כשלושה חודשים, הילדים תומכים בו, מתגורר. לבד בבית פרטי. הגיע לייעוץ עקב ירידה קוגניטיבית. הוא דיווח שבחודשיים האחרונים הוא מרגיש ירידה בזיכרון טווח קצר – שוכח איפה שם חפצים, שואל שוב ושוב את אותה שאלה. בנוסף מתקשה להת. רכז בקריאה או בטלוויזיה ברקע: סוכרת, יתר לחץ דם ויתר שומנים בדם, מ/א אירוע מוחי איסכמי קל ללא חסרים. נוירולוגיים. מאוזן מבחינת מחלות הרקע תחת טיפול תרופתי. מבחן MMSE - תמונה מספר 3 עברה שנה והמטופל הגיע למרפאה למעקב. בדיקת MMSE היתה 28/30. איזה טיפול סביר שקיבל?
o: מעכבי אצטיל כולין
נוגדי דיכאון
קנאביס רפואי
תרגול קוגניטיבי
explanation:
Late-life depression can impair attention, encoding and recall. Symptoms developing after a loss merit a mood assessment alongside evaluation for vascular, degenerative and other cognitive disorders.
**An antidepressant for a depressive episode is the most plausible treatment among the options, given the improvement from MMSE 24 to 28.**

**A. Cholinesterase inhibitor.** The vignette does not demonstrate progressive Alzheimer disease. An isolated MMSE change cannot identify a drug response.
**B. Antidepressant.** Recent-onset cognitive complaints, concentration difficulty and improvement on follow-up fit a reversible depressive contribution. Bereavement alone is insufficient to diagnose major depression.
**C. Medical cannabis.** Cannabis has no established role in treating this pattern of depressive cognitive symptoms and may impair attention.
**D. Cognitive training.** Training can help selected skills but does not specifically treat an underlying depressive episode. Continued cognitive follow-up remains appropriate.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1008–1012, 1014

q: בן 75, מאושפז במחלקה לתשושי נפש. לאחרונה סבל מאצירת שתן, הוכנס צנתר לדרכי השתן, הוחל טיפול ב-DUODART וזקוק לביקור אצל אורולוג לצורך החלטה על גמילה או. ניתוח מה חלוקת הסמכויות בין הגופים בטיפול בחולה זה?
o: קופת החולים מממנת את התרופה, שקיות השתן והביקור אצל האורולוג
המוסד מממן את התרופה ושקיות השתן ומזמין על חשבונו ביקור של אורולוג
המשפחה קונה את התרופה ושקיות השתן וקופת החולים מממנת את הביקור אצל האורולוג
קופת החולים מממנת את התרופה ושקיות השתן והמשפחה מממנת את הביקור אצל האורולוג
explanation:
מגורים במחלקת תשושי נפש אינם מבטלים חברות בקופת חולים. רופא המוסד מטפל ומפנה, והקופה אחראית לשירותי הסל שבאחריותה.
**קופת החולים מממנת את התרופה, ציוד ניקוז השתן והייעוץ האורולוגי לפי הזכאות בסל.**

**א. הקופה אחראית לשלושתם.** תרופות, ייעוץ מומחה וציוד רפואי כלול הם רכיבים נפרדים שסידור המגורים אינו מבטל.
**ב. המוסד משלם על הכול.** תיאום ההפניה, המעקב והטיפול היומיומי בידי צוות המוסד אינם הופכים אותו למבטח של השירותים.
**ג. המשפחה קונה תרופה ושקיות.** מגורים במחלקה אינם מחייבים רכישה פרטית של תרופה וציוד המכוסים בסל.
**ד. המשפחה משלמת לאורולוג.** ייעוץ מומחה בהפניית המוסד מוסדר דרך קופת החולים.

אסמכתא · משרד הבריאות, נוהל 0.4.4, סעיפים 4.2.1, 4.2.3, 4.2.5 ו־5. חוזר פיקוח על קופות החולים 8/2011, ציוד מתכלה בסל.
ref: קשרי בית חולים גריאטרי סיעודי עם קופות החולים

q: בת 75 התקבלה למחלקת סיעוד מורכב לאחר אשפוז ממושך בגין דלקת ריאות, הנשמה, ושהייה בטיפול נמרץ. בקבלתה למחלקה פצע לחץ מעורב בעכוז, בגודל 10x9 ס"מ עם רקמה נמקית מרובה ואודם ניכר סביבו, ראה תמונה מספר 1. במעבדה נצפית עליית מדדי דלקת. איזה גישת הטרייה המומלצת ביותר עבורה?
o: מכנית
אנזימטית
אוטוליטית
כירורגית
explanation:
Debridement restores access to viable tissue by removing necrotic material. A large wound with extensive necrosis, surrounding erythema and inflammatory changes needs rapid assessment and removal of the devitalized burden.

**Surgical debridement is the most suitable approach.** It can remove extensive necrosis promptly and expose pockets or infected tissue for further treatment.

**A. Mechanical debridement.** Wet-to-dry methods may strip viable tissue and cause pain. They are a poor way to achieve prompt control of extensive necrosis.
**B. Enzymatic debridement.** A topical enzyme gradually breaks down nonviable tissue. It is useful in selected stable beds or as an adjunct after sharp removal.
**C. Autolytic debridement.** Endogenous enzymes under an occlusive dressing act slowly. Extensive necrosis and untreated infection are contraindications.
**D. Surgical debridement.** Sharp excision provides the quickest access to a viable bed, especially when infection may be spreading around a large necrotic wound.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 695–696.

q: לפי המאמר Dementia prevention, intervention, and care: 2024 report of the Lancet standing Commission מאת Livingstone et al, מה מהבאים נכון?
o: אלל ApoE4 הוא גורם סיכון משמעותי לדמנציה ואין אפשרות להפחתת סיכון זה בהתערבות חיצונית
ישנם 14 גורמי סיכון הניתנים לשינוי, התערבות ושיפור בהם מפחית סיכון לדמנציה במעל 60%
מעכבי כולין אסטרז לא הראו יעילות משמעותית בהאטת התקדמות דמנציה של מחלת אלצהיימר, ובשל תופעות לוואי משמעותיות עדיף שלא להשתמש בהם
במטופלים עם דמנציה על רקע מחלת גופיפי לווי (Lewy Body), יש לבדוק ביומרקרים ב-CSF על מנת לאשר את האבחנה
explanation:
Inherited susceptibility and modifiable exposures contribute to dementia risk together. A person cannot change which APOE alleles they inherited, but can still address blood pressure, smoking, hearing and other risks.

**APOE ε4 is a significant inherited risk factor.** Its presence does not make the person's overall dementia risk fixed.

**A. APOE ε4 and intervention.** The allele itself stays the same. Calling the carrier's total risk unmodifiable would give the wrong prevention advice.
**B. Fourteen factors reduce risk by more than 60%.** The modeled population fraction was about 45%. It was an estimate of cases potentially delayed or prevented, not an individual treatment effect.
**C. Avoid cholinesterase inhibitors.** Symptomatic benefits are modest but meaningful for some patients. Weigh benefit and adverse effects in established Alzheimer dementia.
**D. Confirm Lewy body dementia with CSF biomarkers.** CSF Alzheimer markers can clarify an Alzheimer contribution when indicated. They are not obligatory confirmation of Lewy body dementia.

Reference · Livingston et al., Dementia Prevention, Intervention, and Care, Lancet Standing Commission 2024, p. 573.

Key note: The exam's wording may imply that no intervention lowers risk for an APOE ε4 carrier. The Commission states, “Risk is modifiable irrespective of APOE genetic status.”
ref: Livingston et al. Dementia prevention, intervention, and care: 2024 report of the Lancet standing Commission. Lancet 2024;404:572–628. · p. 573

q: מה מהבאים מהווה גורם לאוסטיאופורוזיס שניוני?
o: היפרתירואידיזם
מין – אישה
קורס של 5 ימים של PREDNISONE 30 mg
סוכרת שאינה תלויה באינסולין
explanation:
Secondary osteoporosis is bone loss attributable to an underlying disease or drug. **Hyperthyroidism accelerates bone turnover and is a recognized endocrine cause of secondary osteoporosis.**

**A. Hyperthyroidism** Excess thyroid hormone increases remodeling and can produce net bone loss. TSH and thyroxine help identify it.
**B. Female sex** Sex is a background risk factor for primary osteoporosis. It is not a secondary endocrine disorder.
**C. Five days of prednisone** Long-term or repeated glucocorticoid exposure can cause important bone loss. A single five-day course is a poor fit for the chronic exposure described in this comparison.
**D. Non–insulin-dependent diabetes** Type 2 diabetes can increase fracture risk even when DXA looks reassuring. In hyperthyroidism, accelerated remodeling causes net bone loss; diabetes-related fragility can coexist with normal or high measured bone density.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 768–769, Table 51-3. Malaysian Ministry of Health, Management of Osteoporosis 2022, Table 2-1, p. 28.
Key note: Hazzard Table 51-3 names hyperthyroidism. The Malaysian guideline explicitly lists both thyrotoxicosis and type 2 diabetes among secondary causes, so the diabetes option is also clinically defensible.

q: An older adult taking metformin is acutely hospitalized with a major illness causing decreased tissue perfusion. Which treatment decision and reason follow Hazzard?
o: Continue metformin because its low hypoglycemia risk favors use during poor perfusion
Withhold metformin because its hypoglycemia risk becomes the main concern during poor perfusion
Withhold metformin because poor tissue perfusion creates a risk of lactic acidosis
Continue metformin because its peripheral insulin effects compensate for poor tissue perfusion
explanation:
Lactic acidosis is a rare but serious risk of metformin in a patient with tissue hypoperfusion. A low risk of hypoglycemia says little about this separate metabolic complication.

**Withhold metformin because poor perfusion raises the risk of lactic acidosis.** Reassess perfusion and kidney function as the acute illness improves.

**A. Continue because hypoglycemia is rare.** This focuses on the wrong adverse effect during a low-flow illness.
**B. Withhold for hypoglycemia risk.** The action is appropriate, but metformin does not usually cause hypoglycemia in monotherapy.
**C. Withhold for lactic acidosis risk.** Hypoperfusion supplies the precipitating factor that changes the drug's safety profile.
**D. Continue for peripheral insulin effects.** Improved glucose uptake cannot compensate for inadequate tissue perfusion or the danger of acidosis.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p1576.

q: מה מהבאים אופייני למעורבות הפריקרד בחולים אונקולוגיים?

מדידת מרקרים בנוזל לא מסייעת באבחון הנוזל כממאיר
מגיב טוב לטיפול בסטרואידים
keySource: IMA 2024-Sep Basic official answer key after appeals, Q121
explanation:
Cancer-associated pericardial disease can result from malignancy, radiation, drugs or other illnesses. **Fluid cytology can identify malignant cells in malignant effusions, while fluid tumor markers are generally unhelpful**. The denominator matters.

**A. Often presents as tamponade.** Effusions may be asymptomatic. Tamponade can occur but is not the usual presentation of every cancer-associated effusion.
**B. Malignant cells in most cancer patients with pericarditis.** Cytologic yield can be high in malignant effusions. Extending that statement to every cancer patient with pericarditis includes many nonmalignant cases.
**C. Fluid tumor markers are unhelpful.** Routine marker levels do not reliably distinguish malignant fluid. Examine cytology and consider tissue sampling when needed.
**D. Good steroid response.** Treatment depends on cause. A malignant effusion may need drainage and tumor-directed therapy.

Reference · Harrison 22e, p. 587.
Key note: Harrison says about half of symptomatic pericardial disease in patients with cancer is nonmalignant. Cytology is useful in malignant effusions, but the exam also credits a statement applying malignant cells to most cancer patients with pericarditis.

explanation:
Occult giant cell arteritis can cause prolonged inflammatory fever in older adults even without cranial symptoms. At 84 with high CRP and otherwise unrevealing evaluation, **evaluate for GCA, including temporal artery biopsy** among the options offered.

**A. Bone marrow biopsy.** This has a lower yield without specific marrow clues such as multiple cytopenias or an abnormal smear.
**B. Liver biopsy.** A targeted hepatic abnormality or suspicion of granulomatous infection would strengthen the indication.
**C. Temporal artery biopsy.** GCA can present with fever and systemic inflammation without headache, jaw claudication or visual complaints.
**D. Skin biopsy.** No lesion or other skin finding provides a biopsy target.

Reference · Harrison 22e, p. 153.
